# Cross-plane crack coding at 3840x2160: every wall-coder variant priced on the identical published partitions.
#
# base = the published caeBytes. noCross = Hz stripped of its four V taps. baseFix = the published coder with its non-causal tap repaired (see report 09 result 3). hzFirst = code the Hz plane first. interVH / interHV = interleave both planes in one scan. interAsym = interVH with an 8/12 context budget. base12 / inter12 = extra capacity controls.
#
# command : labx wallx (code/lab/crossplane.go)
# Two independent runs agree on every number; only the wall-clock comment differs.
#
# note base: base: Hz context tap {1 1 0} is not causal under this schedule
# note base12: base12: Hz context tap {1 1 0} is not causal under this schedule
# /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-noelruault-go-src-github-com-noelruault/23e7d4b1-17da-4b78-8110-6154f88a8011/scratchpad/hd/src4k.png 3840x2160 — wall coder variants on identical partitions
#   base      ctx 10/10 bits — published caeBytes; Hz reads Hz(x+1,y), which is not causal
#   noCross   ctx 10/10 bits — Hz loses its four V taps: what the existing cross-plane conditioning is worth
#   baseFix   ctx 10/10 bits — baseline with the non-causal Hz(x+1,y) tap swapped for V(x+1,y)
#   hzFirst   ctx 10/10 bits — planes swapped: Hz alone first, then V with both its vertices' Hz members
#   interVH   ctx 10/10 bits — one scan, V then Hz per pixel: V completes its upper vertex, Hz loses its lower one
#   interHV   ctx 10/10 bits — one scan, Hz then V per pixel: V also gets Hz(x,y); Hz keeps only two V taps
#   base12    ctx 12/12 bits — baseline plus two own-plane taps each: capacity control, no new cross-plane information
#   baseAsym  ctx 12/8 bits — twoPassV with a 12-bit V context and an 8-bit Hz context, fully causal
#   interAsym ctx 8/12 bits — interVH with an 8-bit V context and a 12-bit Hz context — same model count as baseAsym
#   inter12   ctx 12/12 bits — interVH with twelve taps per plane
